description:
Redwood Inference is launching an opt-in Quantization Profile Library that publishes per-model quantization profiles and lets customers enable them at the route level (and optionally by region/deployment tier) to reduce inference cost while preserving quality and meeting latency SLOs. The project’s primary goals are: (1) define a stable, versioned quantization-profile schema per model variant (including hardware/precision constraints), (2) safely expose route-level enablement controls via config APIs and Console, (3) integrate the runtime to select and apply an approved profile deterministically, (4) build evaluation and quality guardrails to prevent regressions, and (5) support a staged rollout with observability, rapid rollback, and clear documentation. Scope includes model registry changes (profile storage, validation, compatibility matrices), control plane policy evaluation (route config, tenant overrides, fallback behavior), serving runtime integration (profile loading, kernel selection, memory/caching interactions), Console UX and auditability (change history, previews, canary toggles), and DevEx docs/SDK notes. Out of scope for v1: fully automated per-customer profile recommendation, auto-tuning in production, or default-on enablement across all routes/models.

Key stakeholders: Applied ML (profile generation + evals; Arjun Desai, Karthik Iyer, Jonas Weber), Serving Runtime (execution correctness/perf; Mateo Alvarez, Sofia Ivanova, Hiro Tanaka, Noah Patel), Platform Control Plane + Routing (route config/policy; Priya Natarajan, Ethan Park, Mina Haddad, Ravi Menon), Console & Tooling (UI/workflows; Dylan Brooks, Chloe Martin, Jada Williams), DevEx (docs + SDK guidance; Alex Martinez, Monica Patel), SRE/Release Engineering (rollout + monitoring; Connor O’Brien), and Customer Success/Sales for early design partners.

Planned phases and deliverables: (1) Discovery/design (schema, safety constraints, threat model, rollout plan); (2) Implementation (registry + APIs + runtime selection + Console controls); (3) Validation (offline eval harness, perf suite, canary in perf-canary); (4) Beta with 2–3 design partners (hosted + dedicated), with explicit enable/disable per route; (5) GA (docs, support playbook, ongoing profile publishing cadence). Constraints: profiles must be auditable and reversible; selection must be deterministic; default behavior must remain unchanged when feature is off; and the platform must guard against enabling incompatible profiles for a model/hardware/sequence-length regime. Success metrics: measurable cost/token reduction on targeted models, no statistically significant quality regression on Redwood prompt sets beyond agreed thresholds, stable p95 latency, and low operational overhead (fast rollback, clear debugging signals).

files.description: Published overview of the quantization profile library: goals, terminology, profile lifecycle (authoring→validation→publish→deprecate), and ownership boundaries between Applied ML, Runtime, and Platform.

Formal schema definition for v1 profiles (fields for model_id, variant, quant_method, weight/act precision, calibration set references, hardware constraints, known caveats) with examples and validation rules.
Quality policy for quantization changes: required eval suites, acceptable deltas by task family, statistical methods, and automatic block/rollback triggers.
Playbook for running route-level A/B evals comparing baseline vs quantized profiles, including sampling strategy, metrics, and how results gate rollout.
ADR capturing the decision to use route-level toggles (not global tenant defaults) for v1; includes trade-offs, safety considerations, and deprecation strategy.
Serving standard describing compatibility checks (model/hardware/sequence length), fallback behavior (baseline precision), and how routing should behave under incompatibility.
System doc for the control-plane service endpoints and policy evaluation path that store and resolve route-level quantization settings; includes data model, caching, and audit logging.
Runtime design for selecting and applying a quantization profile: load path, determinism guarantees, kernel selection interactions, and observability signals.
Benchmark plan and standard workloads for measuring cost/token, throughput, VRAM impact, and tail latency with profiles across key GPU SKUs.
Operational rollback runbook: disabling at route level, global kill-switch, identifying impacted tenants, and verifying recovery using dashboards.
PRD for the feature: user stories (ML Eng + platform teams), API requirements, Console UX requirements, rollout plan, and success metrics.
Internal doc outlining how public docs will explain enabling profiles per route, limitations, troubleshooting, and best practices for evals.
